page_title: On the Performance of Cloud-based ARM SVE for Zero-Knowledge Proving Systems

sources.entry: On the Performance of Cloud-based ARM SVE for Zero-Knowledge Proving Systems - One SVE workload run on Graviton 3, Graviton 4, Yitian and Axion with compiler, runs and spread stated.

summary.title: On the Performance of Cloud-based ARM SVE for Zero-Knowledge Proving Systems
summary.one_liner: Cloud ARM CPUs (Graviton4, Axion) currently lag x86-64 AVX512 servers on Merkle tree building for zero-knowledge proofs, mainly due to 128-bit vectors and lower clock speeds, but 512-bit SVE could close the gap while keeping a price advantage.
takeaways: Graviton4 and Axion are 1.6X and 1.4X slower than the latest AMD EPYC and Intel Xeon AWS servers (AVX/AVX512) when building a Merkle tree with over four million leaves.
The ARM gap is attributed to 128-bit vectors versus 512-bit AVX512 and to lower clock frequency.
ARM SVE/SVE2 is described as at least as powerful as AVX/AVX512 and more flexible.
The authors estimate that 512-bit SVE vectors would let ARM CPUs outperform x86-64 while keeping their price advantage (at least 10% cheaper).
summary.summary: The paper benchmarks Polygon's zkProver Merkle tree construction (Poseidon hashes over the Goldilocks field) on cloud ARM servers versus x86-64 servers from AWS and GCP. It compares the AVX/AVX512 vectorized x86 code against ARM SVE/SVE2 implementations on Graviton4 and Axion, and attributes the performance gap to vector width and clock frequency. The authors conclude that ARM SVE is capable but current 128-bit hardware is not competitive, and they estimate that 512-bit vectors would change this. The listing notes a companion measurement across Graviton 3, Graviton 4, Yitian and Axion, but the page itself gives only the abstract.
